cards.text: Moses, Israel's leader, is up on Mount Sinai inside the cloud, and he stays there forty days and forty nights (Exodus 24:18). That's where the LORD speaks to him. First order of business: tell the Israelites to bring Him an offering.

cards.question: God wants an offering from the Israelites. Who is Moses supposed to receive it from?

answers.text: Anyone whose heart moves him to give
Each man who is twenty or older
The leaders of the twelve tribes

cards.text: Then God lists what they can bring: gold, silver and bronze, colored yarn, fine linen, goat hair, leather, acacia wood, olive oil, spices and gemstones. Gold, silver, bronze and then GOAT HAIR, friend, and I love that the goat made the same list as the gold.

cards.question: God tells Moses the Israelites are to make Him a sanctuary so that He may ___ among them.
God tells Moses to design the tabernacle and its furnishings however he thinks best.

cards.text: First up: an ark of acacia wood, overlaid with pure gold inside AND out. Not just the outside, friend, this is not a gold-on-the-front-only kind of job.
God tells Moses to cast four gold rings for the ark's feet, two on each side. Then come poles of acacia wood, and yes, friend, the poles get covered in gold too.

cards.question: The gold-covered poles slide into the rings on the sides of the ark. What are they for?
Once the poles are in the ark's rings, they get pulled out whenever the ark is set down.
God also tells Moses to place something inside the ark. What goes in?

answers.text: The Testimony God will give Moses

cards.text: Next comes a mercy seat of pure gold, the same length and width as the ark, with a cherub of hammered gold at each end. Hammered gold, friend, and I press dough for a living, so I respect anybody who presses harder than me.

cards.question: The two cherubim and the mercy seat are all made from ___ piece of gold.
The cherubim on the mercy seat face away from each other, looking out toward the people.

cards.text: Then the mercy seat goes right on top of the ark, and the Testimony goes inside. I've packed a LOT of boxes with this mustache, friend, and I still get choked up watching something go in a box.

cards.question: God points to a place above the mercy seat, between the two cherubim over the ark. What does He say will happen there?

cards.text: Next piece of furniture: a table of acacia wood, covered in pure gold, with a rim, a gold molding and four gold rings at its legs. Acacia wood and pure gold again, friend, this tabernacle has a THEME.

cards.question: Like the ark, the table gets gold-covered poles of acacia wood so it can be carried.

cards.text: God also wants plates, dishes, pitchers and bowls for the table, all of pure gold. Plates. Dishes. Pitchers. Bowls... ALL gold, friend, and I'd be scared to wash any of it.

cards.question: What are the gold pitchers and bowls for the table used for?
God tells Moses to place something on the table before Him. What is it?
The Bread of the Presence stays on the table before God at ___ times.

cards.text: Then comes a lampstand of pure hammered gold, from its base and shaft right up to its cups, buds and petals. Buds and petals, friend, on a LAMP, this thing is blooming.

cards.question: The lampstand is built from separate gold parts that get joined together.

cards.text: It gets six branches, three on each side, with cups shaped like almond blossoms on every branch and on the lampstand itself. I tried to count all these blossoms on my mustache, friend, and I ran out of mustache.

cards.question: God tells Moses to set seven lamps on the lampstand so they ___ the area in front of it.

cards.text: Even the wick trimmers and their trays are pure gold, and the lampstand and all its tools come from a talent of gold. The wick trimmers, friend, fine, but the TRAYS they sit on are pure gold too.

cards.question: To wrap it up, God gives Moses one more reminder about all of it. What is it?

answers.text: Finish the work in forty days
Let only the priests build it

cards.text: And that's where we'll leave it for now. God's not done talking, friend, and Moses is still up on that mountain.

findings.problem: "Gold, silver, bronze and then GOAT HAIR" says goat hair comes right after bronze. In the list, blue, purple and scarlet yarn and fine linen come between them (Exodus 25:3-4), so what Papa Dorin points out isn't true.

rule.text: Noticing: What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: The joke "I've packed a LOT of boxes with this mustache, friend, and I still get choked up watching something go in a box" doesn't click. It's unclear why putting something in a box would make anyone emotional, so a stranger would likely say "huh?"

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: Most of the jokes are one gag repeated: noticing that something else is gold too. This shows up in stop 1 card 6 ("not a gold-on-the-front-only kind of job"), stop 1 card 7 ("yes, friend, the poles get covered in gold too"), stop 2 card 3 ("ALL gold") and stop 2 card 11 ("the TRAYS they sit on are pure gold too"). Several of these restate the fact without a real punchline, so they read as mild rather than laugh-out-loud.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: Exodus 25:40 repeats the instruction from Exodus 25:9, which was already asked on stop 1 card 5: make everything according to the pattern God shows. Asking about it again tests a repeated line, and the question's wording ("one more reminder") points straight back to it.

rule.text: When a line repeats, like a psalm's refrain, ask about it only the first time it appears.

findings.problem: "Building plans, like the tabernacle or the temple" are listed as a long stretch. A long stretch gets one summary card and never a choice card. Almost all of Exodus 25 is tabernacle building plans (25:10-39), yet the walkthrough asks many choice cards about construction details, such as the poles staying in the rings, which way the cherubim face, one piece of gold, and the seven lamps. Following the rule strictly would shrink the whole passage to about one card.
findings.question: When a whole passage is mostly a long stretch, such as the tabernacle instructions in Exodus 25-31, should it be summed up in a few story cards? Or can its key items (the ark, the mercy seat, the table, the lampstand) and their stated purposes, such as "I will meet with you there" (25:22) and "before Me at all times" (25:30), get choice cards? If so, which details are fair to ask about?
